decisionNodes.stem: Which paired interpretation best fits {patientName}'s record?

answerChoices.label: Reduced cardiac filling; increased respiratory elastic load
answerChoices.rationale: Smaller filling volume with preserved ejection fraction supports reduced preload rather than a new loss of contractility. The increased plateau pressure at the same delivered volume supports an elastic-load component.

answerChoices.label: Reduced cardiac contractility; increased respiratory elastic load
answerChoices.rationale: The respiratory interpretation fits. Smaller end-diastolic volume with similar ejection fraction does not best support primary loss of contractility as the explanation of lower stroke volume.

answerChoices.label: Reduced cardiac filling; increased respiratory resistive load
answerChoices.rationale: The filling interpretation fits. A new resistive load does not by itself account for the higher plateau pressure under the supplied ventilation controls.

answerChoices.label: Reduced cardiac contractility; increased respiratory resistive load
answerChoices.rationale: Both are real contributors to perioperative deterioration, but neither is the best primary account of the supplied paired observations.

decisionNodes.explanation: The fall in stroke volume accompanies a smaller end-diastolic volume with a similar ejection fraction, supporting reduced filling rather than new primary contractile failure. Higher plateau pressure at unchanged tidal volume and PEEP indicates an increased elastic pressure requirement. The reversible pressure sequence fits abdominal venous-return restriction and respiratory mechanical restriction, without proving a unique vascular lesion or excluding every mixed mechanism.

decisionNodes.stem: Which next investigation should be requested for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography
answerChoices.rationale: The residual cholestatic abnormalities keep ductal stone disease in the diagnostic assessment despite the settled episode and absence of a visible duct stone. Noninvasive MRCP can address that question.

answerChoices.label: Hepatobiliary scintigraphy
answerChoices.rationale: This would address continuing concern about acute gallbladder inflammation, but the current symptom/inflammatory pattern and residual laboratory question do not make that the best unresolved target.

answerChoices.label: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography
answerChoices.rationale: Therapeutic ERCP is a real pathway for a confirmed duct stone, but the supplied record has not established a stone or another direct therapeutic indication.

decisionNodes.explanation: The settled episode and gallbladder observations do not establish continuing acute cholecystitis. Persistent cholestatic abnormalities leave a duct-stone question despite no stone being seen on ultrasound. MRCP provides noninvasive assessment before committing to a therapeutic duct-clearance pathway. EUS can also be an appropriate confirmatory study; scintigraphy addresses a different unresolved gallbladder question.

decisionNodes.stem: Which duplex request should accompany {patientName}'s vascular referral before another intervention is selected?

answerChoices.label: Reflux mapping of the superficial and deep leg veins
answerChoices.rationale: The recurrent posterior and medial distributions plus an incomplete connection map do not identify a single treatment target. A complete reflux map can distinguish residual axial, tributary and deep-system contributions.

answerChoices.label: Obstruction mapping of the superficial and deep leg veins
answerChoices.rationale: A broad venous examination is tempting, but a thrombus/outflow protocol does not supply the reflux connections needed to select treatment for these recurrent superficial symptoms.

answerChoices.label: Reflux mapping of the visible calf tributaries
answerChoices.rationale: The largest cluster is a tempting target, but surface prominence does not establish its feeding trunk or explain the additional medial distribution.

answerChoices.label: Obstruction mapping of the visible calf tributaries
answerChoices.rationale: Local venous obstruction can cause tender visible veins, but restricting both the purpose and territory this way does not resolve the recurrent connected-reflux question.

decisionNodes.explanation: The existing sheet shows reflux but does not establish its source and connections. Recurrent varicosities after a partial prior treatment need a reflux assessment that addresses both distributions, remaining superficial connections and the deep system before another target is chosen. Restricting the request to either the previous procedure or the largest visible cluster risks treating an incomplete map.

decisionNodes.stem: Which axillary procedure should be planned for {patientName} at this operation?

answerChoices.label: Left sentinel-node biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: The left specimen is a mastectomy despite retention of the skin envelope. Concurrent sentinel-node staging is ordinarily appropriate there; the right procedure is uncomplicated breast conservation.

answerChoices.label: Right sentinel-node biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: This applies staging to the conserving side while omitting the side whose operation can compromise later mapping. The core diagnosis is the same on both sides, but the operations differ.

answerChoices.label: Left and right sentinel-node biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: The bilateral diagnosis tempts symmetric staging, but uncomplicated pure-DCIS breast conservation does not routinely require sentinel-node biopsy.

answerChoices.label: No sentinel-node biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: Pure DCIS and unremarkable nodal imaging do not remove the conventional staging consideration accompanying the left mastectomy.

decisionNodes.explanation: Retaining the left skin envelope does not make removal of the gland a breast-conserving operation. Sentinel-node biopsy is ordinarily performed with that mastectomy because later mapping may be unreliable. The right localized excision is breast conservation, where routine axillary surgery for pure DCIS is generally omitted. The bilateral core diagnosis therefore does not imply bilateral axillary surgery.

decisionNodes.stem: Which paired conclusion should be carried into {patientName}'s anaesthetic review?

answerChoices.label: Position-associated reduction in filling; acidemia not demonstrated
answerChoices.rationale: The filling change reverses with position at fixed pressure. The CO2/pH directions are compatible with an acidifying change, but the later pH is within the laboratory interval, not acidemic.

answerChoices.label: Position-associated reduction in filling; respiratory acidemia demonstrated
answerChoices.rationale: The filling interpretation fits, but a lower pH that remains within the laboratory interval does not establish acidemia.

answerChoices.label: Pressure-associated reduction in filling; acidemia not demonstrated
answerChoices.rationale: The gas conclusion fits. Assigning the reversible change to a pressure increase is not supported when pressure stays fixed and position is reversed.

answerChoices.label: Pressure-associated reduction in filling; respiratory acidemia demonstrated
answerChoices.rationale: This pair overstates both the pressure attribution and the absolute gas conclusion. Neither follows from the supplied sequence.

decisionNodes.explanation: The smaller filling and stroke volumes reverse on returning flat at unchanged pressure, supporting a positional contribution. CO2 rises and pH falls, but both later measurements lie within their laboratory intervals. That direction of change does not establish acidemia. The earlier low-CO2/high-pH state matters: describing a change as acidifying is different from diagnosing a later acidemic state. These controlled observations do not prescribe a ventilator or fluid adjustment.

decisionNodes.stem: Which imaging study should be prioritized to investigate the source of {patientName}’s cortisol findings?

answerChoices.label: Noncontrast adrenal CT
answerChoices.rationale: The repeated biochemical pattern supports an ACTH-independent branch, so the incidental pituitary focus does not redirect the evaluation. The existing contrast-only abdominal acquisition has not supplied the unenhanced adrenal assessment.

answerChoices.label: Dedicated pituitary MRI
answerChoices.rationale: The small focus is an anchoring temptation. Pituitary localization belongs to an ACTH-dependent evaluation; repeatedly suppressed ACTH does not support making that focus the source here.

answerChoices.label: Contrast-enhanced chest CT
answerChoices.rationale: A search for an ectopic ACTH source can be relevant in an ACTH-dependent pathway. The supplied hormone pattern instead directs adrenal evaluation; neither the incidental adrenal size nor the pituitary image substitutes for that classification.

decisionNodes.explanation: First establish that the current question follows abnormal cortisol assessment rather than screening an image. This does not select adrenalectomy, diagnose the nodule from its size, or establish a universal ACTH-dependent localization sequence.

decisionNodes.stem: Which empagliflozin schedule should be agreed for {patientName}'s next procedure?

answerChoices.label: Continue interruption until ERCP with oral-recovery restart
answerChoices.rationale: The next fasting procedure is too near to restart safely now; restarting afterward depends on recovered intake and clinical state.

answerChoices.label: Resume until ERCP morning with oral-recovery restart
answerChoices.rationale: The eventual recovery condition is appropriate, but resuming until the procedure morning fails the recorded advance interruption requirement.

answerChoices.label: Continue interruption until ERCP with glucose-triggered restart
answerChoices.rationale: The preprocedure interruption fits, but a glucose rise does not establish recovery of intake and clinical state.

answerChoices.label: Resume until ERCP morning with glucose-triggered restart
answerChoices.rationale: This combines inadequate advance interruption with a restart criterion that does not establish postoperative recovery.

decisionNodes.explanation: Reconcile both procedures rather than treating the first recovery as the end of the medication problem. Empagliflozin labeling advises interruption for at least three days when possible before surgery or a procedure associated with prolonged fasting. A new dose 48 hours before the next fasting procedure would interrupt that protection. After the second procedure, resumption again depends on clinical stability and oral intake, not glucose in isolation.

decisionNodes.stem: Which next investigation should guide {patientName}'s persistent postoperative drainage?

answerChoices.label: Arrange hepatobiliary-contrast magnetic resonance cholangiography
answerChoices.rationale: Persistent bile plus a duct segment outside the filled endoscopic tree requires an anatomical study that can map upstream segments and localize excreted biliary contrast, rather than assume the filled main duct represents every source.

answerChoices.label: Arrange repeat endoscopic retrograde cholangiography contrast study
answerChoices.rationale: Repeating injection from the same downstream lumen can again fail to show a source outside the communicating filled tree.

answerChoices.label: Arrange hepatobiliary scintigraphy for leakage
answerChoices.rationale: This can demonstrate activity of a leak but provides less spatial information for the branch relationship needed before another intervention.

decisionNodes.explanation: Do not equate a main-duct injection without visible escape with absence of every biliary source. The drainage and the nonrepresented segment create an anatomical question that the same downstream injection may not answer. Hepatobiliary-contrast MRCP can localize leakage and evaluate duct relationships before the team selects a minor-leak stent or a different HPB pathway. The schematic does not itself prove a particular repair or mandate an operation.
